text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"Boston, MA","level":"city","category":"screening_restrictions","status":"in_force","title":"Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND)","requirement":"Covered housing providers may not use a blanket policy denying housing to anyone with arrests or convictions and must consider applicants case by case. When determining eligibility or considering eviction, they may not consider: arrests that did not result in conviction (including dismissed charges and diversion programs); convictions subject to judicial relief (expungement, sealing, certificates of relief from disabilities); juvenile records; or convictions more than 5 years old. The criminal-history limits do not apply where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought, or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the safety of others, and they do not apply to current criminal behavior. Providers weigh factors such as rehabilitation, time elapsed and age at conviction. Credit: the agent agrees not to use the applicant's credit score to approve or deny applications. Credit history may be used only in lieu of rental history, when rental history is unavailable, to judge ability to pay. Lack of credit history, as opposed to poor credit history, is not sufficient grounds for rejection. Providers are encouraged to use DCJIS to validate CORI, to assign consistent staff, and to offer an appeals process when feasible.","key_value":"Excludes non-conviction arrests, expunged or sealed convictions, juvenile records and convictions over 5 years old; no use of credit score","coverage_conditions":"Housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or with income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
